explanation: Children recited the alphabet ending 'X, Y, Z, and per se and', meaning that the sign & by itself is and. The sign began as a joined form of Latin et.

claims.text: The name 'ampersand' comes from 'and per se and', recited after Z at the end of the alphabet.
The names asterisk, at sign and hash sign do not come from 'and per se and'.
Schoolchildren once ended the alphabet with '& per se and', meaning that the sign & by itself is the word 'and'; the word ampersand is recorded from 1837.
The & sign began as a ligature of the Latin word et, 'and'.
